findings.title: Role limits a list or watch by resourceNames
findings.cause: container watcher exits because the API server refuses its ServiceAccount app: it may not list configmaps in namespace kd-rbac-resourcenames-list. Role settings-reader grants get, list, watch on configmaps only for resourceNames ["settings"], and a list request names no object, so a rule with resourceNames never allows it; its log says: "Error from server (Forbidden): configmaps is forbidden: User \"system:serviceaccount:kd-rbac-resourcenames-list:app\" cannot list resource \"configmaps\" in API group \"\" in the namespace \"kd-rbac-resource…"; Deployment config-watcher has 0 of 1 replicas ready

evidence.what: container watcher exited with code 1 (Error), restarted 6 times
last lines of container watcher's log (run that exited)
evidence.detail: Error from server (Forbidden): configmaps is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:kd-rbac-resourcenames-list:app" cannot list resource "configmaps" in API group "" in the namespace "kd-rbac-resourcenames-list"

evidence.what: Role settings-reader, bound by RoleBinding app-settings-reader: apiGroups [""], resources ["configmaps"], verbs ["get", "list", "watch"]
evidence.command: kubectl get role settings-reader -n kd-rbac-resourcenames-list -o jsonpath='{.rules}'

evidence.what: RoleBinding app-settings-reader grants Role settings-reader to ServiceAccount app

findings.fix: Grant list on configmaps in a rule of Role settings-reader without resourceNames (it then covers every configmap of the namespace), or have the app get settings by name, which the rule allows.
